name: Ghamidi Center of Islamic Learning
mission: To educate people about moral, ethical, and human values as taught in Islam. We aim to separate history and culture from religion and teach it in its purest form as a field of study rather than as a creed.
theoryOfChange: The Ghamidi Center of Islamic Learning, an initiative of Al-Mawrid U.S., has a published 'Strategic Plan for Al-Mawrid United States Inc. Current as of September 13, 2022 Executive Summary' available on GuideStar. This document outlines high-level objectives and action steps, aiming to provide a research and educational environment where Islamic religious thought can evolve and be revisited, teaching Islam as a form of knowledge based on reason and logic. The strategic plan details action steps such as translating research, supporting further research projects, educating children and adults through online and on-premises courses, creating audio/visual content, disseminating content through social media, reaching out to local communities, and providing forums for students to be critical and ask questions. Additionally, the 'About' page on ghamidicenter.com lists 'Our Objectives' as strategic priorities, including promoting engagement with the Qur'an, educating communities on foundational beliefs, supporting scholars, and encouraging institutions for Islamic learning. Al-Mawrid US also operates under a structured governance model with a governance framework established by its Bylaws, ensuring decisions align with its mission, vision, and academic integrity.

rich_narrative.summary: The Ghamidi Center of Islamic Learning (GCIL) is a Texas-based educational organization that provides religious instruction focused on reason, logic, and objective thinking. <cite id="3">Founded in 2019</cite>, the organization offers structured learning tracks, including <cite id="4">an Arabic language program</cite>, weekend Sunday school, and video series. In FY2024, GCIL reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $816,038</cite> while maintaining <cite id="1">a program expense ratio of 75.2%</cite>. The organization holds <cite id="1">an overall score of 71.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite> and is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite>, designated primarily under the fisabilillah category. Operational expenses remain structured around curriculum development and digital outreach, serving an estimated 300 direct beneficiaries. The center operates with moderate fundraising efficiency, spending $0.13 per $1 raised in FY2024.
